description:
According to the palace's own history page, Wiejce began in the early 18th century, when the Kwilecki counts established the estate and built a country house. The estate belonged to the Kingdom of Poland until the partitions of the 1790s, passed to Prussia after 1793, returned briefly to Poland in 1807–1815, and then went back to Prussia.

In 1830 the Kwilecki counts sold it to the Gorajski family, who sold it in 1860 to the Jena-Kothen family; they built the central part of the palace and many of the estate's buildings and cottages. The estate then went to the Lobecke family, which held it until the 1890s, when the Raetzoll family bought it. The von Benninngsen family owned it until 1945, and in the 1930s Aleksander von Benninngsen added wings and turrets and enlarged the park to stretch to the Warta river.

The palace stands in a park at a bend of the Warta river, with a pond system and old trees, and is now a hotel and conference centre. This chronology follows the palace's own history page.

faqs.question: Who built Wiejce Palace?
faqs.answer: According to the palace's own history page, the Kwilecki counts built a country house on the estate in the early 18th century, and the Jena-Kothen family built the central part of the palace after 1860.

faqs.question: What was added to the palace in the 1930s?
faqs.answer: Aleksander von Benninngsen added the wings and turrets and enlarged the park to stretch to the Warta river, according to the palace's own history page.
